title: Electrostatics
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: State Gauss's Law in electrostatics and its formula.
cards.a: The total electric flux Φ through any closed imaginary Gaussian surface equals (1 / ε₀) times the net charge enclosed inside the surface: Φ = ∮ E · dA = q_enclosed / ε₀.
cards.hint: Charges outside the Gaussian surface contribute zero net flux through the closed surface.

cards.q: Electric field E due to an infinitely long straight charged wire of linear charge density λ?
cards.a: E = λ / (2 π ε₀ r), where r is radial distance from wire.
cards.hint: Notice E ∝ 1/r (decreases inversely with distance, unlike point charge which decreases as 1/r²).

cards.q: Electric field E due to a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet of surface charge density σ?
cards.a: E = σ / (2 ε₀).
cards.hint: Remarkable property: E is completely INDEPENDENT of distance r from the sheet (uniform field)!

cards.q: Electric field E of a uniformly charged spherical shell of radius R and charge Q?
cards.a:
Outside (r > R): E = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (Q / r²)
On Surface (r = R): E = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (Q / R²) = σ / ε₀
Inside (r < R): E = 0.
cards.hint: Inside a charged conducting sphere/shell, electric field is identically ZERO (electrostatic shielding).

cards.q: Electric potential V inside a uniformly charged conducting spherical shell of radius R?
cards.a:
Inside (r ≤ R): V = constant = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (Q / R) (equal to potential on surface).
Outside (r > R): V = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (Q / r).
cards.hint: Since E = -dV/dr = 0 inside, potential V does not change from surface to center!

cards.q: Electric potential V and Electric Field E due to an electric dipole of moment p?
cards.a:
Potential at (r, θ): V = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (p cos θ / r²)
Field on Axis (θ = 0°): E_axis = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (2 p / r³)
Field on Equator (θ = 90°): E_eq = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (p / r³).
Ratio: E_axis = 2 E_eq.
cards.hint: Dipole electric field decreases as 1/r³ (much faster than point charge 1/r²).

cards.q: Torque and Potential Energy of an electric dipole in a uniform electric field E?
cards.a:
Torque: τ = p × E ⇒ τ = p E sin θ (maximum at θ = 90°).
Potential Energy: U = - p · E = - p E cos θ.
Stable equilibrium: θ = 0° (U = -pE, minimum).
Unstable equilibrium: θ = 180° (U = +pE, maximum).
cards.hint: Work done in rotating dipole from θ₁ to θ₂: W = p E (cos θ₁ - cos θ₂).

cards.q: Capacitance of a Parallel Plate Capacitor with air vs dielectric medium?
cards.a:
Air medium: C₀ = ε₀ A / d
With dielectric of constant K completely filling space: C = K · C₀ = K ε₀ A / d.
cards.hint: Inserting a dielectric always INCREASES capacitance by a factor of K (K ≥ 1).

cards.q: Capacitance of parallel plate capacitor with dielectric slab of thickness t < d?
cards.a:
C = ε₀ A / [ d - t (1 - 1 / K) ].
If a conducting metal slab of thickness t is inserted (K = ∞): C = ε₀ A / (d - t).
cards.hint: Inserting a conducting slab reduces effective plate separation to (d - t).

cards.q: Battery Connected vs Battery Disconnected: Effect of inserting dielectric K?
cards.a:
1. Battery DISCONNECTED (Q is constant):
   Charge Q: constant | Potential V: V₀ / K | Field E: E₀ / K | Capacitance C: K C₀ | Energy U: U₀ / K.
2. Battery CONNECTED (V is constant):
   Potential V: constant | Charge Q: K Q₀ | Field E: constant | Capacitance C: K C₀ | Energy U: K U₀.
cards.hint: #1 MHT-CET and Board MCQ topic! Memorize whether battery remains connected or disconnected.

cards.q: Formulas for Energy stored in a charged capacitor?
cards.a:
U = (1/2) C V² = (1/2) Q V = Q² / (2 C).
Energy density (energy per unit volume of electric field): u = (1/2) ε₀ E².
cards.hint: SI unit of energy is Joule (J); energy density is J/m³.

cards.q: Capacitors in Series vs Parallel: Formulas and charge/voltage distribution?
cards.a:
Series: 1 / C_s = 1 / C₁ + 1 / C₂ + ... | Charge Q is SAME on all; V_total = V₁ + V₂.
Parallel: C_p = C₁ + C₂ + ... | Voltage V is SAME across all; Q_total = Q₁ + Q₂.
cards.hint: For two capacitors: Series C_s = (C₁ C₂) / (C₁ + C₂); Parallel C_p = C₁ + C₂.

cards.q: Loss of electrostatic energy when two charged capacitors C₁ (at V₁) and C₂ (at V₂) are connected together?
cards.a:
Common potential: V = (C₁ V₁ + C₂ V₂) / (C₁ + C₂)
Energy Loss: ΔU = [ C₁ C₂ (V₁ - V₂)² ] / [ 2 (C₁ + C₂) ].
cards.hint: ΔU is always ≥ 0 (energy is always lost as heat and electromagnetic radiation during charge redistribution).

cards.q: What is an Equipotential Surface and its key properties?
cards.a:
A surface having the same electric potential at every point.
Properties: (1) Work done in moving a charge between any two points on it is ZERO (W = q ΔV = 0).
(2) Electric field lines are always PERPENDICULAR to the equipotential surface.
(3) Two equipotential surfaces NEVER intersect.
cards.hint: For a point charge, equipotential surfaces are concentric spheres centered on the charge.

cards.q: Relation between Electric Field E and Electric Potential V?
cards.a:
E = - dV / dr (Electric field is the negative gradient of potential).
In Cartesian: E = - [ (∂V/∂x) i + (∂V/∂y) j + (∂V/∂z) k ].
cards.hint: Negative sign indicates that electric field points in the direction of STEEPEST DECREASE of potential.

cards.q: Electrostatic Potential Energy of a system of two point charges q₁ and q₂ at distance r?
cards.a:
U = (1 / 4π ε₀) · (q₁ q₂ / r).
For three charges: U = (1 / 4π ε₀) · [ (q₁ q₂ / r₁₂) + (q₂ q₃ / r₂₃) + (q₁ q₃ / r₁₃) ].
cards.hint: Substitute charges with their PROPER SIGNS (+ or -)! If like charges, U > 0; if opposite, U < 0.

cards.q: Mechanical force per unit area (electrostatic pressure) on a charged conductor?
cards.a: f = dF / dA = σ² / (2 ε₀) = (1/2) ε₀ E² (directed normally outwards).
cards.hint: Electrostatic pressure always acts outwards, tending to expand the charged conductor.

cards.q: What is Polarization of a dielectric P and Electric Susceptibility χ_e?
cards.a:
Polarization P: Induced electric dipole moment per unit volume (P = p_net / V). SI unit: C/m².
Relation: P = ε₀ χ_e E, where χ_e is electric susceptibility.
Dielectric constant: K = 1 + χ_e.
cards.hint: Polar molecules (HCl, H₂O) have permanent dipoles; non-polar (O₂, H₂, CO₂) acquire induced dipoles in an external field.

cards.q: Principle of Van de Graaff Generator?
cards.a:
1. Action of points (corona discharge): Charge escapes rapidly from sharp pointed conductors.
2. When a charged conductor is brought in internal contact with a hollow conductor, all charge transfers to the OUTER surface, regardless of outer sphere potential.
cards.hint: Can generate huge potentials up to several million volts (MV).

cards.q: If n small mercury droplets each of radius r, charge q, capacitance C, and potential V coalesce into a single large drop, what are the new values?
cards.a:
Radius: R = n^(1/3) r
Charge: Q = n q
Capacitance: C' = n^(1/3) C
Potential: V' = n^(2/3) V
Stored Energy: U' = n^(5/3) U.
cards.hint: Top MHT-CET shortcut! Potential increases by n^(2/3), Energy increases by n^(5/3).

cards.q: Capacitance of an isolated spherical conductor of radius R?
cards.a:
C = 4 π ε₀ R.
For Earth (R = 6400 km = 6.4 × 10⁶ m): C = 4π ε₀ (6.4 × 10⁶) ≈ 711 μF.
cards.hint: Shows that even a planet-sized conductor has capacitance of less than 1 millifarad!

cards.q: Work done in moving a test charge q₀ around a closed loop in an electrostatic field?
cards.a:
W = ∮ E · dr = 0 (strictly ZERO).
Because electrostatic force is a CONSERVATIVE force.
cards.hint: Work done is independent of the path taken and depends only on initial and final positions.

cards.q: Force between two parallel plates of a capacitor?
cards.hint: Notice factor of 1/2! One plate is in the field E/2 produced by the other plate alone.

cards.q: Dielectric Breakdown and Dielectric Strength?
cards.a:
Dielectric Breakdown: The phenomenon where an insulator ionizes and becomes conducting under very high electric fields.
Dielectric Strength: Maximum electric field an insulator can withstand without breakdown (for air ≈ 3 × 10⁶ V/m).
cards.hint: SI unit of dielectric strength is V/m.

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor vs near a thin charged sheet?
cards.a:
At surface of a conductor: E = σ / ε₀ (perpendicular to surface).
Near an infinite thin sheet of charge: E = σ / (2 ε₀).
cards.hint: Conductor field is TWICE as strong because charge resides on two surfaces (or interior field is 0).
